description: `(or false true (1 / 0))` — the parenthesized variadic form — left-associates and short-circuits exactly like the infix form: it stops at the second (`true`) operand, so `1 / 0` is never evaluated and no `ol-div-zero` fires. Issue #95. Issue #815: the operand was `:missing` until the check before execution landed, at which point an unbound read became a *statically* decided fault and this correct program stopped running at all. `1 / 0` keeps the subject and strengthens it — the skipped operand is one that would genuinely raise (`ol-div-zero`) if it were evaluated, and its absence from the diagnostics is the proof.
